name: Guy Fawkes

attributes.attribute: the night of the yearly rite
a neighbor of it in time
keep a memory of older festival fires

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A folk night in Britain holds the name of Guy Fawkes. In 1605 he led a plan to destroy the English Houses of Parliament. The plan failed, and the night became a yearly memory of that fall. Men light bonfires and burn an image on the fifth of November. The date sits near the old feast that opened the winter. Some say those fires stand in the place of the old festival fires.

okr.objective: Read the folk night of Guy Fawkes against the old feast of winter.
key_results: Tell the plot of 1605 against Parliament.
Fix the yearly rite on November 5.
Note the old feast that opened the winter.
Keep the bonfire beside the older fires.
